issues.description: Basic usage example uses `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` which obscures intent and is not idiomatic
issues.detail: The line `training_node = next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is equivalent to `pipeline.nodes[0]` (or `next(iter(pipeline.nodes))`) but harder to read. For documentation aimed at teaching a new feature, the reader's cognitive budget should be spent on the preview API, not on parsing a redundant generator expression. Prefer `training_node = pipeline.nodes[0]` or filter by name explicitly: `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes if n.name == 'train_model_node')`. Literate code teaches; this snippet distracts.

issues.description: `node(...)` calls appear as bare top-level statements with no surrounding `Pipeline([...])` context
issues.detail: In the Mermaid customisation, Text-with-syntax-highlighting, and `make_preview_fn` examples, the docs show `node(func=..., preview_fn=..., name=...)` as a free-floating statement. A careful reader will copy this and find it does nothing useful — `node()` returns a `Node` object that must be placed inside a `Pipeline([...])`. The earlier Basic usage example does it correctly; later examples should either mirror that, or annotate `# inside Pipeline([...])`. As written, the snippets are not runnable as shown, which violates the literate-programming contract that example code should be followable by a careful reader without ambiguity.
issues.lines: Mermaid section (`node(func=process_data, ...)`); Text preview section (`node(func=calculate_metrics, ...)`); closure section (`node(func=process_data, ...)`)

issues.description: Contradictory guidance about data access in preview functions
issues.detail: The 'Using preview functions with data context' section states: 'Preview functions don't have access to node inputs or outputs directly. They're independent functions that you define. If you need to generate previews based on actual data, you can use closures or access datasets within the preview function.' The closure example then captures a hard-coded `sample_data` literal at pipeline-construction time — which is not 'actual data' from the run. The reader is told two contradictory things (use closures; access datasets) and shown neither end-to-end. State the invariant: when is `preview_fn` called, what state can it observe, and which patterns are sanctioned? Without that, the section is under-specified.
issues.lines: 'Using preview functions with data context' subsection

issues.description: Lifecycle of `node.preview()` is never specified — when is it called, who calls it, what does it cost
issues.detail: The doc tells the reader to attach `preview_fn` and call `node.preview()`, but never answers the fundamental questions a serious reader needs: Is `preview_fn` called eagerly at pipeline construction, lazily on `.preview()`, or only by Kedro-Viz? Is it called once per run, on every viz refresh, never during `kedro run`? Does it run in the same process? The 'Make previews fast' best practice hints at frequent invocation but doesn't say. Without an invariant for when the function runs, the reader cannot reason about side effects, caching, or the 'access datasets within the preview function' suggestion above.

issues.description: `ImagePreview` example has two `return` statements in one function
issues.detail:
```python
def preview_correlation_matrix() -> ImagePreview:
    # Can return a URL
    return ImagePreview(content="https://example.com/correlation_matrix.png")
    # Or a data URI for inline images
    # return ImagePreview(content="data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...")
```
The second `return` is commented out so it's not a bug, but the pattern reads awkwardly. Prefer two separate small functions (`preview_from_url`, `preview_from_data_uri`) or a single function with a clear `if/else`. Small thing, but the page has six other examples and consistency helps the reader.

issues.description: Mermaid `custom_config` example mixes Mermaid native config with a Kedro-Viz-specific `textStyle` key without flagging the distinction
issues.detail: The example puts `securityLevel`, `flowchart`, and `themeVariables` (all real Mermaid config keys) next to `textStyle` (which the comment describes as 'CSS styling for text nodes'). The reader cannot tell which keys are passed to Mermaid and which are interpreted by Kedro-Viz's renderer. The footnote links to the Mermaid schema for 'a complete list of available Mermaid configuration options', which implies all keys are Mermaid keys — but `textStyle` is not in the Mermaid schema. State the invariant: which keys are Mermaid-native and which are Kedro-Viz extensions, and what happens to unknown keys.

issues.description: TextPreview meta `language` accepted values are under-documented
issues.detail: The doc says 'Kedro-Viz supports `python`, `javascript`, and `yaml` highlighting.' What happens for unsupported values — silent fallback to plain text, error, raw output? A careful reader writing `meta={'language': 'sql'}` deserves to know. One short sentence on the fallback behaviour closes the gap.

issues.description: Checklist admits 'Added tests to cover my changes' is unchecked, and there is no testable example in the docs
issues.detail: This is a docs-only PR so test coverage of code is not in scope, but the 'Test preview functions' best practice tells readers to test their preview functions without showing how. A 6-line example using `assert isinstance(node.preview(), JsonPreview)` would make that best practice actionable. Knuth's stance: tests complement proofs; if you tell the reader to test, show them the shape.

issues.description: Stray blank `style.yml` exception entry and `ignore.txt` addition for lowercase `polars` lack context
issues.detail: Adding `JSON` to headings exceptions and lowercase `polars` to ignore.txt are reasonable for the new prose, but no comment explains why `polars` is now ignored separately from the existing `Polars`. A one-line note in the PR description (or a commit message) would prevent a future maintainer from reverting it as a duplicate. Minor.

issues.description: `!!! warning` admonition path link to experimental policy is relative and may break depending on docs builder
issues.detail: `[docs/about/experimental.md](../about/experimental.md)` — the bracketed display text is the absolute repo path while the target is a relative path from `docs/build/nodes.md`. If the docs site renders with a different root or the file is moved, the link silently rots. Recommend a single canonical form (either both relative, or use a docs-builder cross-reference). Small literate-programming hygiene item.
issues.lines: Warning admonition at top of new section

review.summary: Docs-only PR adding a comprehensive page on node `preview_fn`. The page is well-structured and covers each preview type with a runnable-looking example, which is the right shape for literate documentation. The main rigor gaps are around invariants the reader needs to reason about the feature: when `preview_fn` is invoked, what state it can observe, and the precise contract for `meta` (Mermaid-native vs Kedro-Viz extensions, supported `language` values, fallback behaviour). Several later code blocks show `node(...)` as a free-floating statement outside any `Pipeline([...])`, which a careful reader will copy and find non-functional. Decision: UNDER-AUDITED / NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT — the content is correct in spirit but the explanation needs tightening before this becomes the reference page for an experimental feature.
